import numpy as np

def r_rowSums_dist(x, na_rm=False):
    """
    Compute row sums of a dist object.
    
    Parameters:
    x : numpy array or scalar
        A condensed distance matrix (upper triangle of symmetric matrix in row-major order)
    na_rm : bool
        If True, ignore NaN values when summing
    
    Returns:
    numpy array
        Row sums of the distance matrix
    """
    # Handle scalar input
    x = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(x, dtype=float))
    
    # Calculate n from condensed form length: len = n(n-1)/2
    if len(x) == 0:
        return np.array([])
    
    n = int((1 + np.sqrt(1 + 8 * len(x))) / 2)
    
    # First pass: identify which rows have NaN values (when na_rm=False)
    rows_with_nan = set()
    if not na_rm:
        idx = 0
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                if np.isnan(x[idx]):
                    rows_with_nan.add(i)
                    rows_with_nan.add(j)
                idx += 1
    
    # Second pass: compute row sums
    row_sums = np.zeros(n)
    idx = 0
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n):
            dist_val = x[idx]
            
            if na_rm:
                if not np.isnan(dist_val):
                    row_sums[i] += dist_val
                    row_sums[j] += dist_val
            else:
                row_sums[i] += dist_val
                row_sums[j] += dist_val
            
            idx += 1
    
    # Set rows with NaN to NaN (when na_rm=False)
    if not na_rm:
        for row_idx in rows_with_nan:
            row_sums[row_idx] = np.nan
    
    return row_sums
